summary: Batairt Student Transit Holdings, Inc. (client, Buyer) is acquiring all outstanding shares of Kestrelbrook Student Transportation, Inc., a Delaware school bus operator running about 420 buses under district pupil transportation contracts, from Fapul Family Transportation Holdings, LLC (Seller). The Stock Purchase Agreement is dated October 6, 2026 and closes October 30, 2026. The purchase price of $48,500,000 is paid partly by a $7,000,000 Seller Note issued by Buyer. The ancillary documents are a key employee agreement with Kestrelbrook's COO, a transition services agreement under which Seller keeps providing driver background-check, drug-testing and routing services, a Buyer board consent, an IP assignment of routing software from Seller to the Company, and a side letter on district change-of-control consents. The folder also holds a pre-deal mutual NDA and a bus depot lease estoppel certificate. Four issues are planted, all adverse to Buyer. (1) The TSA makes Buyer indemnify Seller, without any cap, for service-related losses, including losses caused by Seller's own negligence. (2) The SPA's Pre-Closing Tax indemnity is tied by cross-reference to the 12-month general survival period, and claims require a filed proceeding. (3) The Seller Note picks New York law and Manhattan courts, while the SPA picks Delaware law and the Court of Chancery. The SPA's precedence clause lets the Note control set-off disputes, which splits the forum for Buyer's set-off remedy. (4) The side letter redefines 'Material District Contract' for the SPA's consent-loss indemnity as three listed contracts. That list leaves out the two contracts the SPA's own Schedule 4.4 shows require district change-of-control consent.

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: Two TSA provisions combine to give Buyer unlimited exposure. TSA Section 8.2 requires Buyer, as Recipient, to indemnify Seller, as Provider, for all Losses arising from or relating to the Services. The Services are driver background checks, drug and alcohol testing administration, and route planning. The indemnity expressly covers Losses caused by Provider's negligence. TSA Section 8.4 caps only Provider's liability, at the fees paid, and states that it does not limit Recipient's obligations under Section 8.2. The SPA's Article IX cap in Section 9.5 applies only to indemnification under that Article. SPA Section 11.12 also makes each Ancillary Agreement control as to its own subject matter. Nothing in the folder therefore caps this obligation. Delaware enforces indemnity for the indemnitee's own negligence when the language is express, as it is here. Buyer would bear uncapped liability, including student injury claims, if Seller negligently processes a driver background check or drug test.
detect_terms: including Losses caused by Provider's negligence
shall not limit Recipient's obligations under Section 8.2
issues.expected_finding: Under TSA Sections 8.2 and 8.4, Buyer must indemnify Seller without any cap for all Losses relating to the Services, including Losses caused by Seller's own negligence in driver screening and testing. The SPA cap does not reach this obligation. Buyer should strike the negligence coverage, make the indemnity mutual and fault-based, and cap it.

issues.label: indemnity survival gap
issues.description: Three SPA provisions combine to cut off the tax indemnity early. SPA Section 9.2(b) gives Buyer a special indemnity for Pre-Closing Taxes, which include payroll and fuel excise taxes on the Company's driver workforce. Section 9.1(c) says the Section 9.2(b) obligation survives 'for the same period as the representations in Section 4.10'. Section 4.10 (Taxes) is not among the Fundamental Representations defined in Section 1.1. It therefore falls under the 12-month general survival period in Section 9.1(a), which expires October 30, 2027, measured from the October 30, 2026 Closing Date stated in Section 3.1. Section 9.1(e) also bars any claim unless a Proceeding is commenced before the period expires; a notice of claim is not enough. Taxing authorities normally have three years or more from the filing of a return to assess. Delaware enforces shortened survival periods under 10 Del. C. § 8106(c). The tax indemnity will therefore expire long before most pre-Closing tax exposures can surface.
detect_terms: for the same period as the representations in Section 4.10
issues.expected_finding: Sections 9.1(c) and 9.1(a) tie the Pre-Closing Tax indemnity to the 12-month general survival period, which ends October 30, 2027. Section 9.1(e) also requires suit to be filed before then. Buyer should extend tax indemnity survival to 60 days after the applicable statute of limitations and allow claims to be preserved by written notice.

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: Seller Note Section 10 chooses New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in the Borough of Manhattan. The Note says payments are subject to Buyer's set-off rights under the Purchase Agreement. The SPA chooses Delaware law in Section 11.8 and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery in Section 11.9. SPA Section 9.7 lets Buyer set off indemnifiable Losses against Seller Note payments. SPA Section 11.12, however, provides that each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its subject matter. Each document looks ordinary on its own. Read together, any dispute over whether Buyer properly withheld a Note payment falls under the Note's New York law and Manhattan forum. Meanwhile, the underlying indemnity claim must be brought in Delaware. Seller could sue on the Note in New York, potentially by summary judgment in lieu of complaint, while Buyer's indemnity claim proceeds in Chancery. This splits Buyer's main recourse across two forums and risks inconsistent results.
detect_terms: laws of the State of New York
issues.expected_finding: The Seller Note's New York law and Manhattan forum conflict with the SPA's Delaware law and Chancery forum. Under SPA Section 11.12, the Note controls disputes over Buyer's Section 9.7 set-off, so set-off and indemnity claims would be split across two forums. Buyer should conform the Note to Delaware law and the Chancery forum, or make the SPA control set-off disputes.

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: SPA Section 1.1 defines 'Material District Contract' as any school district pupil transportation contract with annual revenues over $500,000. SPA Section 9.2(d) uses that term to indemnify Buyer if a district terminates a Material District Contract for lack of change-of-control consent. SPA Schedule 4.4 identifies the Pellbrook Unified School District and Ashcombe County Public Schools contracts as above the threshold and requiring district consent to the change of control. Side letter Section 2 provides that references to Material District Contracts in Section 9.2(d) mean only the contracts listed on Annex A. Annex A lists three other district contracts and omits Pellbrook and Ashcombe. Under SPA Section 11.12, the side letter controls as to its subject matter. The side letter reads as an ordinary consent-cooperation letter on its own. Combined with the SPA, it removes from the consent-loss indemnity the two contracts that actually need consent.
issues.expected_finding: The side letter narrows 'Material District Contract' for SPA Section 9.2(d) to the three Annex A contracts. Because the side letter controls under SPA Section 11.12, the Pellbrook and Ashcombe contracts that Schedule 4.4 shows require change-of-control consent fall outside the consent-loss indemnity. Buyer should delete the redefinition or add those contracts to Annex A.
